reasons: The idea deserves compute; the rules need fixing first. The mechanism is economic and new here: a scheduled surprise that hits a crowded leveraged-fund book forces risk-limit selling spread over hours. It is judged as an asymmetry between three arms that trade the same surprises in the same direction at the same cost. It is not a duplicate. edge_hunt traded the first-move direction on 92 NFP days with no surprise size or positioning (12 NFP cells, best t +0.53, which supports the near-zero neutral expectation). cot_positioning used positioning alone. cb_drift found no decision-day drift. The family is theory-set (24 cells, 8 in the hypothesis arm, within the 36 limit).

Rule bug, d0 exit before entry: the d0 target is 20:30 UTC on the release date, but NZD releases come at 21:45/22:45 UTC. On NZDUSD 77 of 668 qualifying releases (design+check, |dz| >= 1, with a COT rank) fill at or after 20:30 UTC. In design at q 0.8, z 1.0 that is 14 against, 10 with and 22 neutral releases. As written, the causal fallback marks every bar from the earlier target onward, so these become one-bar trades filled at the New York rollover spread.

Rule bug, overlap: the leftover guard exit[sig_k] closes the previous trade at the open of the next release's fill bar. But the executor registers an entry only when it is flat at the signal bar's close (executor.py, 'register this bar's signals' block), so the new release is not traded either. Overlapping holds are cut short with nothing in their place. This hits 10-30% of d1 releases (EURUSD q 0.8, z 1.0 design: against 15 of 101, with 21 of 113, neutral 45 of 172), and the arms then differ for a mechanical reason.

Counts and dates are off. The leveraged-fund (TFF) series in cot.parquet starts on 2010-07-20 (as-of), so the first 52-row rank is usable on 2011-07-15. Design trades therefore run 2011-07 to 2017-12, 6.5 years; 2010 has none. The EURUSD neutral counts in the brief (235 / 303 / 127) count releases with no rank as neutral. The rules skip those, which gives 172 / 240 / 94. The against and with counts match (101/113, 69/77, 49/51). The q 0.9, z 1.5 against cell has 32 releases and can never reach the 40-trade minimum.
Kill-rule typos: rule (1) speaks of 12 'against' cells, but the grid has 8 (crowd_q x z_min x hold). Rule (4), '4 of the 8 design years', has to count only years that have trades.

Power: on EURUSD alone each arm has about 85-160 trades. With an R standard deviation of about 0.8, the against-minus-with difference has a standard error of about 0.1 R, so the +0.08 R asymmetry gate barely tells real from noise. Pooled over the six markets (about 565-630 against trades after de-overlap) the standard error falls to about 0.05 R. The test of the mechanism has to be pooled before anything is promoted.

Trend confound: leveraged-fund crowding follows the trend (in cot_positioning only 16% of crowding fades went with 63-day momentum). So the against arm is mostly counter-trend and the with arm mostly with-trend. In strong-trend years such as EURUSD 2014-15, one day of trend drift is about 0.1 R on a 1 x ATR20 stop, which is the size of the effect being predicted. The asymmetry needs a trend diagnostic to be read.

Speed: the pooled against arm has about 8 trades a month (673 design releases in about 78 months at q 0.8 / z 1.0 over six markets). At +0.12 R that scores about 0.33, and less once you allow for the same US release hitting four or five pairs in the same minute. It needs about +0.25 to +0.3 R to reach 0.7. The second path, 'a timing filter on the parked USDJPY legs', is not pre-registered. This is an edge-recording test.

Costs are low: a 1 x ATR20 stop (EURUSD median 75 pips) against a round trip of about 2 pips is about 0.03 R. The exception is NZDUSD fills at 22:00 UTC from November to March, which sit on the New York rollover (2012-2017 median opening spread 3.8 pips, p90 8.4, against 1.3-1.4 pips at other hours). That adds about 0.04 R to those trades, and the pipeline's G4 gate needs every stage-C market positive at 1.5x costs.
revisions: BUILDER (implement exactly): (R1) Late releases: skip a release entirely (no entry, no markers) unless xi > sig + 1, where xi = the first bar at or after the exit target (E at exit_utc). For d0 this removes NZD releases at 21:45/22:45 UTC and any release whose fill is at or after 20:30 UTC. For d1 it never binds. (R2) Replace the leftover guard with a planned-hold de-overlap. Walk the qualifying releases of the active arm in ts_avail order. Keep a release only if it passes every skip rule and m.ts[sig] >= target_prev, the exit target of the last KEPT release; for the first kept release there is no condition. A dropped release sets no entry and no exit markers. A trade that was stopped early does not reopen the window. For kept releases only, set exit_long[xi_k - 1] = exit_short[xi_k - 1] = True, plus the causal fallback on every bar j with m.ts[j] >= target_k and j <= the sig of the next kept release (m.n - 1 for the last). Drop the separate leftover guard. With this rule the previous trade is closed at or before the open of the next signal bar, so the executor is flat when the next entry registers. (R3) PARAMS and GRID unchanged. DIRECTOR: (R4) After this review, edit specs/auto/fx_surprise_against_crowd.json as the hypothesis says: stage_a = {market: EURUSD, grid: all 24 cells} and grid = {arm: [against], crowd_q: [0.8, 0.9], z_min: [1.0, 1.5], hold: [d0, d1]}. apply_review writes the full 24-cell grid. Left that way, stage B picks each market's best cell from the control arms too, and G2, G2b and G4 would be computed on control cells. (R5) Restate the expectations: design trades start 2011-07-15. EURUSD design releases (against/with/neutral) are 101/113/172 at q 0.8, z 1.0; 69/77/240 at q 0.9, z 1.0; 49/51/94 at q 0.8, z 1.5; 32/33/129 at q 0.9, z 1.5. After R1-R2 the q 0.8, z 1.0 arms have about 98/106/162 trades (d0) and 86/92/127 (d1). (R6) Kill rule (1): 'among the 8 against cells'. Kill rule (4): at least 4 of the 7 years 2011-2017 positive (2011 = July-December only). (R7) Mechanism gate before any promotion: if the against arm passes B/C, run the matching with and neutral cells (same crowd_q, z_min, hold) on GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDJPY and USDCAD with end = 2024-01-01 (design and check only; counted as trials). Rule (2) is then judged on the pooled six-market trades: against minus with >= +0.08 R and against minus neutral >= +0.05 R in design, and both > 0 in check. The EURUSD stage A asymmetry alone is not enough. (R8) Breadth rule (3): give a merged release the news side of the currency with the larger sum of |surprise_z| among its rows. USDCAD has 136 merged USD+CAD releases (simultaneous 12:30/13:30 UTC data); report them also as 'mixed'. (R9) Reporting: each arm's avg R split by whether the trade agrees with the sign of the pair's 63-trading-day close-to-close change at the signal bar; NZDUSD NZD-news fills separately (fill spread in pips and as a share of the stop). (R10) Neutral-arm carry-forward: allowed only as a new hypothesis judged on the five markets where the neutral arm was never run, plus the holdout. Its EURUSD design and check results are spent and cannot count as its evidence. (R11) Strike the 'timing filter on the parked USDJPY legs' path; it is not pre-registered. Speed is judged by the monthly Sharpe of the pooled six-market R per month after costs, which accounts for the same-minute US-news correlation. Below 0.7 the result is recorded as an edge, not traded.
notes_for_builder: 1. Calendar rows: e = F.ext_series(m, 'calendar'). Build the mask with numpy over e.column('impact') == 'high', e.column('time_source') == 'scraped', np.isfinite(e.column('surprise_z')), e.column('currency') in (base, quote), and the case-insensitive exclusions on e.column('event') (None counts as ''). Select with F.ext_subset(m, 'calendar', mask). If no rows survive (the truncation leak test can cut the series), return the empty Signals. Contribution per row = surprise_z x inv x side (inv -1 for the listed unemployment and borrowing names). Group rows with an identical ts_avail; dz = the sum of their contributions. Never rescale dz, and never take a rank, quantile or z-score over the whole sample. 2. COT: c = F.ext_subset(m, 'cot', F.ext_series(m, 'cot').column('market') == ccy), in ts_avail order. rank_r = (count of v[r-rw+1..r] <= v[r]) / rw on spec_net_oi with rw = p['rank_weeks'], NaN for r < rw - 1. For a release at T: j = np.searchsorted(c.ts_avail, T, 'right') - 1; skip the release in every arm when j < 0 or rank_j is NaN. state +1 if rank >= crowd_q, -1 if rank <= 1 - crowd_q, else 0; crowd_pair_dir = cot_sign x state. 3. Raise ValueError on an unknown arm, an unknown hold or an unsupported symbol (cot_sign +1 for EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD; -1 for USDJPY, USDCAD). 4. sig = np.searchsorted(m.close_times(), T + delay_min minutes, 'left'). Skip if sig >= m.n - 1, if close_times[sig] - T > max_delay_min, if m.ts[sig] is on another UTC date than T, or if ATR20[sig] is not finite or <= 0. ATR20 = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, p['atr_n'])) with daily = F.daily_bars(m). 5. Exit target: E = the UTC date of T (d0) or the next Monday-to-Friday date after it (d1); target = E + exit_utc (F.parse_hhmm); xi = np.searchsorted(m.ts, target, 'left'). Keep the release only if xi < m.n and xi > sig + 1 (R1). 6. Planned-hold de-overlap (R2): a Python loop over the releases (a few hundred) is fine. Then set entry and markers for kept releases only: entry_long/entry_short[sig] by dir, entry_type 0, valid_bars 1, sl_dist = sl_atr x ATR20[sig], tp_dist NaN, max_bars 0. 7. Checker expectations, EURUSD design 2011-07 to 2017-12: about 98 (d0) / 86 (d1) trades for arm against, q 0.8, z 1.0; about 106/92 for with and 162/127 for neutral. Releases before 2011-07-15 have no rank and are skipped in every arm. 8. Read every tunable from p (arm, crowd_q, z_min, hold, sl_atr, delay_min, max_delay_min, exit_utc, atr_n, rank_weeks); no hard-coded 52, 15 or 20:30.
